text:
alana: quick heads-up from a micro usability run — a couple of small IA/interaction nits around the compact left rail and deep-links. Two things: 1) gesture area for compact groups is tiny at a few breakpoints (hard to hit on mobile); 2) when opening permalinks the main content focuses but the rail rarely shows the active state, so keyboard users lose orientation.

mike: can you paste steps to repro?

alana: repro: 1) open external link to Console -> Projects -> Models -> Foo -> Revisions 2) page loads, focus lands in main content 3) left rail stays collapsed, no aria-current on rail item 4) tab sequence goes header -> controls -> body with no visible nav highlight. Also on mobile, the chevron tap target is ~34px in compressed spacing.

sara: accessibility quicks: whatever we do must set aria-current="page" on the revealed nav item, ensure it has tabindex and role="link" (or button depending on element), and announce the change via aria-live polite. Respect prefers-reduced-motion for any expand animation.

jess: UX idea: two-tier fix — 1) increase touch target to 48px by expanding hit area (padding) without changing visible compactness; 2) on external deep-links, programmatically reveal minimal ancestor path and set focus to the rail entry but call focus({preventScroll:true}) so the main viewport doesn't jump. For discoverability, show a transient micro-toast: "Reveal in nav" with CTA.

noah: implementation note — router already emits navigation:restored. We can run a small reconcile: find nav node via data-path, expand ancestors, set aria-current, set tabindex=0 and focus with preventScroll, then if the node is not visible inside the rail viewport call node.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}). Also handle drawer mode by opening first.

olivia: small copy suggestion for the toast: "Showing Foo in the left nav — Reveal" (button). If clicked, animate the reveal briefly so users understand relation. If not clicked, keep the nav silent but accessible via keyboard.

sara: also add a short aria-live message: "Navigation: Models > Foo revealed" so screen readers get the state change. Keep it polite. And test with NVDA + VoiceOver.

mike: concern: auto-expanding on every deep-link can be noisy and may override a user's intentional collapse state. Proposal: behave differently for external navigations vs in-app routings — external -> reveal, in-app -> preserve. Also add a user setting in Console preferences "Respect my collapsed nav" default true for logged-in users. For experiments we can default external behaviour to reveal for 5% then ramp.

jess: design tokens: I'll add nav-compact-hitarea and nav-reveal-duration (default 140ms) + motion-reduced fallback. Also will mock two toasts: ephemeral CTA vs silent auto-reveal.

noah: dev tests: unit for aria-current toggling, e2e for deep-link desktop and mobile, a11y smoke to assert live region message. Also add a perf guard: batch DOM writes when expanding multiple levels to avoid layout thrash.

sara: accessibility QA checklist: tabindex order, visible focus outline (not color-only), aria-current present, aria-live message, reduced-motion respected, touch target >=48px on mobile.

alana: decision proposal: implement minimal reconcile on router:restored with focus({preventScroll:true}) + aria-current set, bump mobile hit areas to 48px via token update, and launch a 5% experiment that shows the toast option to reveal vs silent reveal. If experiment shows low CTA engagement, default to silent minimal reveal.

mike: will implement router reconcile and add feature flag. I'll also add integration tests around focus behavior.

jess: I'll update Figma frames and the component spec to include expanded hit areas and micro-animation.

olivia: I'll wire up experiment copy & metrics: nav.reveal.clicked and nav.reveal.source=external|internal.

sara: I'll own accessibility tests and file the a11y bug if anything regresses.

designbot: Figma comment added at https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/compact-rail-reveal (by @jess).

alana: thanks all — I'll open the issue (#5367) with acceptance criteria and tag eng-runtime / router. If no objections Ill proceed with the PR. :thumbsup:
